subject: Decision input: low-latency vs throughput path for FastPay feature
messages:
From: Alex Ford <alex.ford@fastpay.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.r@fastpay.com
Date: 2027-09-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask from today

Karthik, thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick summary from our side and the key ask: we walked through two FastPay product paths — an authorization-enrichment path (very latency-sensitive) and a nightly reconciliation/analytics path (throughput-sensitive).

Numbers we gave on the call:
- Auth enrichment: peak 200 QPS, p95 target <= 40 ms (user-facing), requests are short sequences (<= 64 tokens).
- Analytics ingestion: sustained 15k req/min during batch windows, p95 latency < 5s acceptable, sequences vary up to 1k tokens.

Primary asks:
1) Recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for each path given our constraints.
2) Any pilot sizing or benchmark artifacts you need from us to validate the recommendation.
3) Ballpark timelines and what we should expect for an SLA on the auth path if we pick Dedicated.

Attaching the QPS/p95 snapshot you asked for and the call recording. Happy to hop on a quick follow if easier.

Alex
Head of Product Integrations
FastPay
[attachment: call-recording-20270918.mp3] [attachment: fastpay-qps-p95-snapshot.csv]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ford <alex.ford@fastpay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-18T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask from today

Thanks Alex — good notes and the trace csv is helpful. Looping in Marissa (solutions/ops) and Ben (pricing/solutions) to align on recommendation and next steps.

High-level recommendation (short answer):
- Auth enrichment (200 QPS, p95 <= 40 ms): Recommend Dedicated for the production workload if FastPay needs strict p95 guarantees and isolation. Hosted can work for an initial pilot if you can tolerate some cold-start variability and slightly higher p95 tail during bursts, but Dedicated gives predictable kernels/autoscaling and can be pinned to a GPU pool with tight SLOs.
- Analytics ingestion (high throughput, tolerant latency): Hosted or Dedicated both are viable; Hosted is generally lower friction and cheaper for bursty batch jobs if you can accept shared infrastructure. If data residency/compliance or very consistent throughput is desired, Dedicated or Private would be better.

What we need from you to pick the final path and size a pilot:
- A 48-hour rolling sample of request timestamps + payload size (CSV — we got the one you attached, the richer the better).
- Any compliance/regulatory constraints (PII storage/retention, VPC requirements).
- Target SLOs per endpoint (p50/p95/p99) and acceptable error rates.

Initial pilot suggestion: run auth enrichment on Hosted under a controlled traffic replay for 48 hours to validate p95 behavior, then cut to Dedicated for production if results show p95 > 30 ms under sustained 200 QPS. If you want us to size Dedicated up-front we can propose a small reserved GPU pool (2x A40-style instances with pinned kernels) and run a 4-hour synthetic ramp test.

Ben — can you draft a quick reserved capacity sketch and 3-month pricing delta (pilot vs Dedicated)? Marissa — can you note the benchmarking checklist and any runbook items we should ask FastPay for?

Next step: Alex — are you available for a 30-min follow on Tuesday to confirm which pilot route you want?

—Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-slo-options-20270918.pdf]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, Alex Ford <alex.ford@fastpay.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask from today

Karthik — quick operational notes from my side after reviewing the csv:
- The auth path has tight payload size variance; KV-cache hit rate will matter a lot. We'll want sample traces (anonymized) so our runtime team can estimate prefix reuse.
- For Dedicated sizing: 2 GPU endpoints (pinned) looks reasonable to start for sustained 200 QPS if we target p95 < 40 ms and allow batching window of 8-12 ms. If we need p95 < 30 ms we should consider 3 pinned endpoints or a higher single-GPU class.
- For Hosted pilot: we recommend a replay with incremental ramp (50->100->150->200 QPS) with synthetic user think-time to mimic production burstiness; we should capture p50/p95/p99 + kernel selection logs.

Runbook checklist I'm adding to Drive: sample traces (anonymized), traffic replay script, target SLOs, internal contact for on-call escalation. Will upload the checklist and share link.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: call-notes-tracing-checklist.txt]

From: Alex Ford <alex.ford@fastpay.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, priya.r@fastpay.com
Date: 2027-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask from today

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and aligns with our internal thinking. Quick replies to your asks:
- We'll provision an anonymized 72-hour trace export (events + payload hashed) and share the link by EOD tomorrow.
- Compliance: FastPay needs SOC2 + VPC peering for production. Pilot can run on Hosted if we use token redaction and short retention, but production will require either Dedicated or Private with VPC.
- We're leaning to run the pilot on Hosted to validate behavior quickly, then migrate the auth path to Dedicated before Q4 GA if benchmarks show host instability at p95.

Next steps:
1) Karhtik — can you send a short pilot runbook and a Dedicated sizing sketch (Ben/Marissa help) by Monday?
2) Marissa — please post the runbook checklist to Drive and share the link in-thread.
3) Ben — initial reserved capacity delta and pilot pricing estimate.

I'll block time for a Tuesday 30-min follow (10:00am PT) — invite incoming.

Regards,
Alex
Head of Product Integrations
FastPay
